rules.title: Tenant Protection Act statewide rent cap (Civ. Code § 1947.12)
rules.requirement: An owner of residential real property may not increase the gross rental rate over any 12-month period by more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest rent charged in the prior 12 months.
rules.key_value: 5% + CPI, or 10%, whichever is lower, per 12 months
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rental property, except housing certified for occupancy within 15 years, owner-occupied two-unit structures, affordable or deed-restricted and subsidized housing, dormitories, and housing under a lower local rent cap.
rules.exemptions: Affordable or deed-restricted and subsidized housing; dormitories; housing under a lower local rent cap; housing certified for occupancy within 15 years; single-family/condo housing alienable from other titles and owned by a non-corporate owner with required notice; owner-occupied two-unit structures; mobilehome owners.
rules.interaction: State cap does not apply to housing under a local rent control ordinance that restricts annual increases below the state cap.
rules.quoted_span: an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase.
rules.conflict_note: The section is operative April 1, 2024, but subdivision (h) says it applies to rent increases occurring on or after March 15, 2019. | Sources disagree: effective_date: D024 says 2024-04-01, D040 says 2024-08-01; key_value: D024 says '5% + CPI, or 10%, whichever is lower, per 12 months', D040 says '5% + CPI, max 10%; 8.9% (Aug 1, 2024–Jul 31, 2025)'

rules.title: California just cause eviction requirement (Tenant Protection Act)
rules.requirement: An owner may not terminate a residential tenancy without just cause stated in the written notice once a tenant has occupied 12 months; no-fault terminations require one month's rent as relocation assistance or a rent waiver.
rules.key_value: Just cause after 12 months' occupancy; 1 month's rent relocation or rent waiver
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential real property after 12 months' continuous occupancy (24 months if new adult tenants added), except housing certified within 15 years, owner-occupied homes up to two units, non-corporate owners of separate-title property, and deed-restricted affordable housing.
rules.exemptions: Transient hotel occupancy; nonprofit hospital, religious, extended-care and residential-care facilities; dormitories; units sharing bathroom or kitchen with owner; owner-occupied single-family residences up to two units; owner-occupied duplexes; housing certified for occupancy within 15 years; alienable separate property with non-corporate owners; deed-restricted affordable housing.
rules.interaction: Local just cause ordinances adopted on or before September 1, 2019, or more protective ones, govern instead of this section.
rules.quoted_span: (a) Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.

rules.title: California security deposit limit and return rules (AB 12)
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge at most one month's rent as a security deposit; qualifying small landlords may charge up to two months. The deposit must be returned with an itemized statement within 21 days after the tenant vacates.
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent; up to 2 months for small landlords
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential tenancies in California; landlords owning only two rental properties with no more than four residential units total may charge up to two months' rent.
rules.exemptions: Landlords owning only two rental properties with no more than four residential units total, where ownership is held by a natural person, family trust or limited liability company of natural persons.
rules.quoted_span: Starting July 1, 2024, many landlords may only charge one month's rent for unfurnished and furnished units

rules.title: California security deposit cap and return requirements
rules.requirement: A landlord may not demand a security deposit above one month's rent (two months for a small natural-person owner), and must return the remainder with an itemized statement within 21 calendar days after the tenant vacates.
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent; 2 months for small natural-person landlords
rules.coverage_conditions: Security for a rental agreement for residential property used as the tenant's dwelling. Natural-person landlords or LLCs of natural persons owning no more than two rental properties totaling four units may take up to two months' rent.
rules.exemptions: Advance payment of six months' rent if the lease term is six months or longer; alterations made by mutual agreement; the one-month cap does not apply to security collected or demanded before July 1, 2024; service members from the two-month limit.
rules.quoted_span: (c) (1) Except as provided in paragraph (2), (3), or (5), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.

rules.title: California application screening fee cap
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent may charge an applicant an application screening fee only when a rental unit is or will be available, may not exceed $30 per applicant (CPI-adjusted annually), and must provide an itemized receipt, refund unused amounts, and deliver the credit report within seven days.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any landlord (owner of residential rental property) or agent and any applicant, including a guarantor or cosigner, requesting to rent a residential unit.
rules.exemptions: No refund is required for an applicant denied after consideration for failing the landlord's established screening criteria.
rules.interaction: Does not preempt federal or state housing assistance program rules on collection of deposits and fees.
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant.
rules.conflict_note: Sources disagree: effective_date: D026 says 2026-01-01, D005 says 2026; key_value: D026 says '$30 per applicant, CPI-adjusted annually', D005 says '$68.96 (2026)'

rules.title: California application screening order and criteria rule
rules.requirement: A landlord charging a screening fee must consider completed applications in the order received, give screening criteria in writing with the application, approve the first applicant who meets the criteria, and charge no fee unless the application is actually considered.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any landlord (owner of residential rental property) or agent and any applicant requesting to rent a residential unit.
rules.quoted_span: Completed applications are considered, as provided for in the landlord’s established screening criteria, in the order in which the completed applications were received.

rules.title: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955 source-of-income, income and credit screening protections
rules.requirement: Landlords may not discriminate based on source of income (including Section 8 vouchers), may not use income standards that disregard a subsidized tenant's actual rent share, and must let applicants substitute alternative proof of ability to pay for credit history.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to owners of any housing accommodation and to the rental of housing in California.
rules.exemptions: Verifying employment, requesting landlord references, and verifying identity remain permitted; inquiring about income level or source is not source-of-income discrimination.
rules.quoted_span:
(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:
(A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.

rules.title: FEHA source-of-income and criminal-history screening protections
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not refuse to rent based on a tenant's source of income, including Section 8 vouchers, and may not impose blanket criminal-history bans or consider arrests without conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to most housing accommodations in California, including single-family and multi-family homes, apartments, condominiums, short-term rentals, mobile homes, subsidized housing, dormitories, sober living, group homes, shelters, and RVs or boats used as homes.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied home renting to one additional person may exclude applicants based on protected characteristics; senior housing and homeless youth housing may be limited by age; a shared single dwelling may be limited to one sex.
rules.citation: California's Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA)
rules.quoted_span: No. California law protects tenants from discrimination based on how a tenant will be paying rent (“source of income”). This includes the State of California’s COVID-19 Rent Relief Program, Housing Choice (Section 8) vouchers, (SSI) social security disability benefits, or wages earned from a job.

rules.title: AB 325 common pricing algorithm prohibition
rules.requirement: It is unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade, or to coerce another person to set or adopt a price or commercial term the algorithm recommends.
rules.coverage_conditions: Any person as defined in Section 16702, excluding the end consumer of a product or service.
rules.exemptions: The end consumer of a product or service is not a “person” for purposes of this section.
rules.quoted_span: (a) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.

rules.title: Massachusetts ban on local rent control (Ch. 40P)
rules.requirement: No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, except a city or town that accepts this chapter may adopt rent control regulation subject to limits, and after six months compliance by property owners becomes entirely voluntary.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rent control regulation by cities and towns; such regulation may not cover evictions, occupancy, services, condominium conversion or removal of properties.
rules.exemptions: Cities or towns that accept this chapter may adopt rent control regulation; that regulation may not apply to units owned by a person owning fewer than ten rental units or units with fair market rent exceeding $400.
rules.interaction: Bars cities and towns from enacting or maintaining rent control; only a municipality that accepts this chapter may adopt rent control regulation.
rules.quoted_span: No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, except that any city or town that accepts this chapter may adopt rent control regulation that provides:

rules.title: Boston rent stabilization authorization (Bill H.3744)
rules.requirement: Would authorize the city of Boston to implement rent stabilization, subject to the approval of the mayor and city council.
rules.coverage_conditions: Would apply to the city of Boston if enacted.
rules.quoted_span: An Act petition for a special law authorizing the city of Boston to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections

rules.title: Determination of lease for nonpayment of rent
rules.requirement: A landlord may terminate a written lease for nonpayment of rent only after giving the tenant 14 days' written notice to quit, and the tenant may avoid termination by tendering all rent due with interest and costs before the day the answer is due.
rules.coverage_conditions: Written leases of residential premises where rent is not paid; the tenant may cure by paying all rent due, interest and costs.
rules.quoted_span: Upon the neglect or refusal to pay the rent due under a written lease, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the lease, unless the tenant, on or before the day the answer is due, in an action by the landlord to recover possession of the premises, pays or tenders to the landlord or to his attorney all rent then due, with interest and costs of suit.

rules.title: Massachusetts notice to determine tenancy at will
rules.requirement: A tenancy at will may be terminated by either party on three months' written notice; where rent is payable at periods of less than three months, notice equal to the interval between payment days or thirty days, whichever is longer, is sufficient. Nonpayment of rent requires fourteen days' written notice to quit.
rules.coverage_conditions: All tenancies at will, wherever the rent reservation is payable.
rules.exemptions: Where the tenant has not received a similar notice within the preceding twelve months, the tenancy is not determined if the tenant pays or tenders all rent due within ten days of the notice.
rules.quoted_span: Estates at will may be determined by either party by three months' notice in writing for that purpose given to the other party; and, if the rent reserved is payable at periods of less than three months, the time of such notice shall be sufficient if it is equal to the interval between the days of payment or thirty days, whichever is longer.

rules.title: Massachusetts anti-reprisal protection for tenants
rules.requirement: A landlord may not threaten or take reprisal against a tenant for protected activity such as reporting code violations or organizing a tenants' union; a termination notice within six months of the activity is presumed retaliatory.
rules.key_value: Damages of 1 to 3 months' rent; 6-month reprisal presumption
rules.coverage_conditions: Any tenant of residential premises who engages in protected activity: enforcing housing laws, reporting health or building code violations, or organizing or joining a tenants' union.
rules.exemptions: A notice of termination for nonpayment of rent is excluded from the six-month reprisal presumption; any waiver of the section in a lease or rental agreement is void.
rules.quoted_span: The receipt of any notice of termination of tenancy, except for nonpayment of rent, or, of increase in rent, or, of any substantial alteration in the terms of tenancy within six months after the tenant has commenced, proceeded with, or obtained relief in such action, exercised such rights, made such report or complaint, or organized or joined such tenants' union

rules.title: Notice to quit for nonpayment of rent — required informational form
rules.requirement: A written notice to quit for nonpayment of rent to a residential tenant must be accompanied by a form covering repayment agreements, rental assistance programs, court rules and eviction restrictions, and stating that the notice is not an eviction. A court may not accept a summary process writ, summons or complaint without proof the form was delivered.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential tenants given a notice to quit for nonpayment of rent, and any court with jurisdiction over summary process actions for residential dwelling units, including the Boston municipal court department.
rules.quoted_span: A notice to quit for nonpayment of rent given in writing by a landlord to a residential tenant pursuant to this chapter shall be accompanied by a form that shall include, but not be limited to: (i) documentation of any agreements between the tenant and landlord for the tenant to repay the landlord for nonpayment of rent; and (ii) information on: (1) rental assistance programs

rules.title: Boston tenant eviction protections authorization (Bill H.3744)
rules.requirement: Would authorize the city of Boston to implement tenant eviction protections, subject to the approval of the mayor and city council.
rules.coverage_conditions: Would apply to the city of Boston if enacted.
rules.quoted_span: By Representative Montaño of Boston, a petition (accompanied by bill, House, No. 3744) of Samantha Montaño (with the approval of the mayor and city council) that the city of Boston be authorized to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections.

rules.title: Massachusetts security deposit cap, interest and return rules
rules.requirement: A lessor may not require a security deposit above the first month's rent, must hold it in a separate interest-bearing account, pay five per cent yearly interest, and return the deposit with an itemized list of deductions within thirty days after the tenancy ends.
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent (deposit cap); 5% interest per year; return within 30 days
rules.coverage_conditions: Rentals of residential real property in Massachusetts; the section sets no building age, size or owner limits.
rules.exemptions: Deposit-transfer liability does not apply to a city or town taking title under chapter 60 or to a foreclosing mortgagee or mortgagee in possession that is a chartered financial institution; a landlord may still recover a deposit for wilful or malicious damage exceeding it.
rules.quoted_span: (iii) a security deposit equal to the first month's rent provided that such security deposit is deposited as required by subsection (3) and that the tenant is given the statement of condition as required by subsection (2);

rules.title: CORI fee waiver for veterans organizations
rules.requirement: No fee shall be assessed for a CORI or self-audit when a veterans organization requests information about employees, volunteers, or veterans for which the organization provides housing.
rules.coverage_conditions: Requests by any veterans organization for a CORI or self-audit relative to employees, volunteers, or veterans for which the organization provides housing.
rules.quoted_span:
no fee shall be assessed for a CORI
           or self-audit where any veterans organization is requesting information relative to employees,
           volunteers, or veterans for which such organization provides housing.

rules.title: Massachusetts limit on upfront amounts a lessor may charge
rules.requirement: At or before the start of a tenancy a lessor or its agent may not require payment beyond first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit equal to one month's rent, and the cost of a key and lock.
rules.key_value: first month's rent + last month's rent + 1 month's rent deposit + key/lock cost
rules.coverage_conditions: Any residential tenancy; the cap binds a lessor or the lessor's agent and applies before or at the commencement of the tenancy.
rules.exemptions: An executive-office regulation may authorize an optional fee in lieu of a security deposit, capped in total at 1 month's rent.
rules.quoted_span:
(b) At or prior to the commencement of any tenancy, no lessor or agent of the lessor may require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay, to the lessor or to an agent of the lessor, any amount in excess of the following:
(i) rent for the first full month of occupancy;  and,
(ii) rent for the last full month of occupancy calculated at the same rate as the first month;  and,
(iii) a security deposit equal to the first month's rent

rules.title: Massachusetts broker fee paid by the party who engaged the broker
rules.requirement: A licensed broker or salesperson may contract only with the prospective tenant or only with the landlord, and any fee may only be paid by the party who originally engaged and contracted with the broker.
rules.coverage_conditions: Any person who, for a fee, finds dwelling accommodations for prospective tenants; that person must be a licensed real estate broker or salesperson.
rules.quoted_span: Any fee shall only be paid by the party, lessor or tenant who originally engaged and entered into a contract with the licensed broker or salesperson.

rules.title: CORI housing screening rules (803 CMR 5.00)
rules.requirement: Landlords, property managers, real estate agents and public housing authorities may request CORI on a housing applicant only as the final step in the application process, must give required notices before adverse housing decisions, and may not retain CORI beyond seven years.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to landlords, real estate agents, public housing authorities, and property management companies that request CORI to screen applicants for the rental or lease of housing, including market rate and subsidized housing.
rules.quoted_span:
CORI shall not be retained for longer than seven years from the last date of residency of the
           housing applicant in the housing unit or the date of a housing decision regarding the housing
           applicant, whichever is later.

rules.title: CORI access for purposes other than evaluating a housing applicant
rules.requirement: Nothing in 803 CMR 5.00 limits a landlord, property management company, real estate agent, or public housing authority from accessing CORI under other sections of 803 CMR 2.00, including as an employer or member of the general public.
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords, property management companies, real estate agents, and public housing authorities that access CORI.
rules.quoted_span:
Nothing in 803 CMR 5.00 shall limit the ability of a landlord, property management
           company, real estate agent, or public housing authority to access CORI pursuant to any other
           section of 803 CMR 2.00: Criminal Offender Record Information (CORI)

rules.title: Massachusetts fair housing source-of-income protection
rules.requirement: A landlord or any person furnishing rental accommodations may not discriminate against a tenant because the tenant receives federal, state, or local public assistance or housing subsidies, including rental assistance or rental supplements.
rules.coverage_conditions: Any person furnishing credit, services or rental accommodations; protects tenants who receive federal, state or local public assistance or housing subsidies.
rules.quoted_span: For any person furnishing credit, services or rental accommodations to discriminate against any individual who is a recipient of federal, state, or local public assistance, including medical assistance, or who is a tenant receiving federal, state, or local housing subsidies, including rental assistance or rental supplements, because the individual is such a recipient

rules.title: Massachusetts deposit-alternative fee must be offered without regard to income or credit
rules.requirement: A lessor that offers a fee in lieu of a security deposit must offer it to every applicant whose application is approved, regardless of income, credit score and other listed characteristics, and may not use those factors to set the fee amount.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies only if the executive office of housing and livable communities promulgates regulations authorizing a fee in lieu of a security deposit, and to lessors who offer such a fee.
rules.quoted_span: (E) require a lessor who offers such a fee in lieu of security deposit:  (I) to offer the option of a fee in lieu of a security deposit to every prospective tenant whose application for occupancy has been approved, regardless of income, race, gender, gender identity, disability, sexual orientation, immigration status, size of household or credit score;  and (II) not to consider such factors and categories when setting the amount of the fee;

rules.title: Bill H.5222, preventing algorithmic rent fixing
rules.requirement: Would prevent algorithmic rent fixing in the rental housing market. The bill was reported favorably by the committee on Housing and referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means on 3/12/2026.
rules.quoted_span: An Act relative to preventing algorithmic rent fixing in the rental housing market

rules.title: Massachusetts S.2983 algorithmic rent-setting ban (proposed)
rules.requirement: Would prohibit algorithmic rent setting in the rental housing market. Reported favorably by the Joint Committee on Housing and referred to the Senate Committee on Ways and Means on March 12, 2026.
rules.quoted_span: An Act prohibiting algorithmic rent setting

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Ordinance annual general adjustment 5% cap (Measure BB)
rules.requirement: A landlord of a fully covered unit may not raise rent by more than the Annual General Adjustment, capped at a maximum of 5%. A landlord may petition for rent increases only for completed capital improvements, not planned ones.
rules.coverage_conditions: Fully covered rental units under the Berkeley Rent Ordinance; new construction certified after 1980, most single-family homes and most condominiums are only partially covered and have no rent ceiling.
rules.exemptions: Units only partially covered by the Ordinance (for example new construction certified after 1980, most single-family homes, most condominiums); unused banked AGAs may still be used.
rules.interaction: Certain government-subsidized units are only partially covered because federal or state law or regulation prohibits rent control.
rules.quoted_span: The maximum AGA is 5%. This means that, if the formula in the Rent Ordinance results in an AGA that is greater than 5%, the AGA approved by the Board for that year can be no more than 5%.

rules.title: Berkeley Annual General Adjustment for 2026 (Regulation 1148)
rules.requirement: Eligible landlords under the Berkeley Rent Ordinance may raise 2025 permanent rent ceilings by 1.0% no earlier than January 1, 2026, subject to the conditions and tenant notice in Rent Board Regulation 1148.
rules.coverage_conditions: Rent-controlled units with 2025 permanent rent ceilings; the increase may not be applied to tenancies that began on or after January 1, 2025 whose rents were set under the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act.
rules.exemptions: Tenancies that began on or after January 1, 2025 whose rents were set pursuant to the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act.
rules.interaction: Excludes tenancies whose rents were set under the state Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act.
rules.quoted_span:
At its regular meeting on October 16, 2025, the Berkeley Rent Stabilization Board 
adopted the Annual General Adjustment (AGA) Order for Year 2026 which will allow 
eligible landlords to increase the 2025 permanent rent ceilings by 1.0% no earlier than 
January 1, 2026.

rules.title: Berkeley 2026 relocation assistance payment adjustment
rules.requirement: Owners who evict tenants for owner move-in or to remove a property from the rental market under the Ellis Act must pay relocation assistance; for 2026 the standard payment is $19,413 and the additional payment for qualifying households is $6,471.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants evicted through owner move-in evictions or Ellis Act evictions under the Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance and the Ellis Implementation Ordinance.
rules.exemptions: Rental units where the tenant shares kitchen or bath facilities with the landlord are exempt only if the landlord lived on the property before the tenant.
rules.quoted_span:
The standard relocation assistance payment will increase to
$19,413
.
The additional relocation assistance payment for qualifying households will increase to
$6,471
.
rules.conflict_note: Sources disagree: key_value: D004 says '$19,413 standard; $6,471 additional (1.5% CPI adjustment)', D006 says "at least 1 month's Fair Market Rent"

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Ordinance security deposit interest
rules.requirement: Landlords of units fully or partially covered by the Berkeley Rent Ordinance must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year, plus a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance.
rules.exemptions: Golden Duplex (owner-occupied duplex); units where the owner shares a kitchen or bath with the tenant if the owner lived on the property when the tenancy started; ADU tenancies started after Nov 7, 2018 where either unit is owner-occupied; university dormitories; nonprofit cooperatives.
rules.quoted_span: For tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year.

rules.title: Berkeley tenant screening and application fee rules
rules.requirement: Before taking a screening fee, an owner must give the applicant a tenant screening fee rights statement and the state fee cap; an owner may not charge an existing tenant a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy or to change a roommate.
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential rental agreements in Berkeley; owners or agents who charge a fee to obtain a consumer credit report to process a rental application.
rules.quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.

rules.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.requirement: Rental housing providers in Berkeley may not ask about or use criminal history or background checks in advertising, applications, tenant selection or decision-making, and may not refuse to rent or terminate a tenancy based on criminal history.
rules.coverage_conditions: All rental housing providers in Berkeley, except listed exemptions.
rules.exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; public housing/Section 8 properties (limited exemptions); owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units where the owner resides as primary residence; units under a rental agreement allowing owners to move back; units occupied by existing tenants seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates.
rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.

rules.title: Berkeley coordinated pricing algorithm ban
rules.requirement: A landlord may not use a coordinated pricing algorithm to set rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in Berkeley, and no one may sell, license or provide such an algorithm to Berkeley landlords.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley and to any person selling, licensing or providing the software to Berkeley landlords.
rules.exemptions: Products that publish rental data aggregated and anonymous without recommending rents, fees or occupancy; products setting rent or income limits under affordable housing guidelines; products used for market research for project financing, appraisals, or research, testing or training for software development.
rules.quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described 
in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in 
the City of Berkeley. Each separate month that a violation exists or continues, and each 
separate residential dwelling unit for which the landlord used the coordinated pricing 
algorithm, shall constitute a separate and distinct violation.

rules.title: Housing Stability Notification Act notice requirement
rules.requirement: A landlord planning to end a tenancy must give the tenant a Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources at the same time as the Notice to quit or Notice of non-renewal, and must submit a Notice to Quit / Non-renewal of Lease Submission Verification Form to the City.
rules.coverage_conditions: All landlords ending a tenancy; foreclosing owners must also submit the verification form.
rules.exemptions: Residences in any hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility; and residences in a non-profit facility whose primary purpose is short-term treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug, or other substance abuse.
rules.quoted_span: The Housing Stability Notification Act requires any landlord to provide renters with a Notice of Tenant’s Rights and Resources when planning to end a tenancy agreement.

rules.title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not impose a blanket denial based on arrests or convictions; they must consider applicants case-by-case and may not consider non-convictions, sealed or expunged convictions, juvenile records, convictions over 5 years old, or credit scores.
rules.key_value: conviction more than 5 years old excluded
rules.coverage_conditions: Housing providers receiving DND funding or land, or with income-restricted units created under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy.
rules.exemptions: Federal or state criminal history requirements that conflict with this policy; convictions with a direct relationship to the housing or an unreasonable risk of harm; current criminal behavior.
rules.interaction: Where federal or state law imposes a conflicting criminal history requirement, that federal or state law preempts this policy.
rules.citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy
rules.quoted_span:
Housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development (DND) funding and/or 
land, or that have income restricted units created under the Boston Planning and Development 
Agency (BPDA) Inclusionary Development Policy will not impose a blanket policy that denies 
housing to anyone with arrests and or convictions.

rules.title: Boston fair housing bar on discrimination against renters using rental assistance
rules.requirement: In Boston it is illegal for a landlord to discriminate when renting housing, including by refusing to rent to a tenant because the tenant uses rental assistance such as Section 8, social security disability, or veterans vouchers.
rules.coverage_conditions: All housing rented, bought, sold, or financed in the City of Boston; the commission investigates complaints under local, state, and federal fair housing laws.
rules.quoted_span:
The landlord tells you they don't accept rental assistance. This includes Section
8 vouchers, social security disability vouchers, and veterans vouchers.

rules.title: Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance source-of-income screening protection
rules.requirement: Landlords, sellers and rental agents may screen applicants only with a reasonable standard applied equally and uniformly to all, and may not discriminate based on source of income, including Section 8 and public benefits.
rules.coverage_conditions: Housing discrimination provisions covering viewing or renting an apartment and terms of tenancy; exemption for 2-family dwellings when the owner lives there.
rules.exemptions: 2-family dwellings when the owner lives there.
rules.quoted_span: Under the law, landlords, sellers and rental agents may use any reasonable standard to determine which applicants are selected, as long as that standard is applied equally and uniformly to all applicants.

rules.title: Hoboken Rent Leveling and Stabilization Ordinance rent control
rules.requirement: Rents are controlled at the October 1, 1985 base rent; no increase may be demanded, paid or accepted except as the chapter allows, and a landlord must give 30 days' written notice before any increase. Excess increases are void and must be refunded.
rules.key_value: base rent as of October 1, 1985; 30 days' notice
rules.coverage_conditions: All dwelling units in Hoboken, except motels/hotels, industrial and commercial property, school and government housing, first rental of newly constructed dwellings, buildings vacant since January 1, 1984, and multiple dwellings constructed after June 25, 1987.
rules.exemptions: Motels and hotels; first rental of newly constructed dwellings; industrial property; nonresidential and commercial property; school, college or institution student housing; state or federal government housing; buildings vacant since January 1, 1984; multiple dwellings constructed after June 25, 1987 (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.1).
rules.interaction: Application of this chapter is preempted while a contract gives a governmental agency authority to regulate rents that supersedes the City's; the chapter resumes when the contract ends.
rules.quoted_span:
All rents for rental of housing space and services in dwellings to which this act is applicable
     are hereby controlled at the base rent level received by the landlord as of October 1, 1985, and
     no rental increases shall be hereinafter demanded, paid or accepted, except as provided in this
     chapter.

rules.title: Hoboken rent control baseline freeze
rules.requirement: A landlord may not charge rent above the level in effect on the chapter's effective date, nor above the rent received on January 11, 1973 where that exceeds the rent authorized by the chapter.
rules.coverage_conditions: All rentals subject to Chapter 155; no building age, size or owner limits stated.
rules.quoted_span:
No landlord shall, after the effective date of this chapter, charge any rents in excess of what he was
     receiving from the effective date of this chapter; nor shall such landlord charge any rents in excess
     of what he was receiving on January 11, 1973, if such excess is in excess of the rental which is
     authorized by this chapter.

rules.title: Hoboken vacancy decontrol 25% initial rent cap
rules.requirement: Upon a registered apartment's vacancy, the new tenant's initial rent may not exceed 25% over the last rent (excluding any capital improvement surcharge), and decontrol requires a voluntary vacancy or legal eviction and may occur no more than once every three years.
rules.coverage_conditions: Registered residential apartments in the city; on vacancy the unit is decontrolled for the new tenant's initial rental, with later increases still governed by the chapter.
rules.exemptions: The new tenant's initial rental is exempt from the chapter's rent controls; any further increase is not.
rules.quoted_span:
the apartment unit shall become decontrolled and exempt
     from the provisions of this chapter for the new tenant's initial rental; provided, however, that said
     rental shall be limited to an increase of 25% over the last rental paid by the tenant who voluntarily
     vacated the rental unit, exclusive of any capital improvement surcharge that is a component of
     said last rental

rules.title: Hoboken rent leveling annual increase cap
rules.requirement: A landlord may not request or receive a rent increase at lease expiration or termination of more than 5% or the CPI differential, whichever is less, and no more than one cost-of-living increase per 12-month period.
rules.key_value: 5% or CPI differential, whichever is less
rules.coverage_conditions: Dwellings subject to the Hoboken Rent Leveling and Stabilization chapter; the cap applies at lease expiration or termination and to periodic tenants and lease terms under one year.
rules.exemptions: Newly constructed dwellings and buildings completely vacant since January 1, 1984, where the rent officials determine eligibility for an exemption as defined in the chapter.
rules.quoted_span:
At the expiration of a lease or at the termination of a lease of a periodic tenant, no landlord
     may request or receive a percentage increase in rent which is greater than 5% or the percentage
     difference between the consumer price index three months prior to the expiration or termination
     of the lease and three months prior to the commencement of the lease term, whichever is less.

rules.title: Hoboken rent increase disclosure over 10%
rules.requirement: Landlords increasing rent by more than 10% upon renewal of a lease with a current tenant must itemize costs, state whether a rent algorithm was used, notify the tenant of the right to take legal action, and give Hoboken Division of Housing contact information before the increase takes effect.
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential landlords in Hoboken seeking to increase rent by more than 10% upon renewal of a lease with a current tenant.
rules.quoted_span: All residential landlords seeking to increase rent by more than 10% upon a renewal of a lease with a current tenant year over year shall be required to make the following disclosures to existing tenants either in the lease upon renewal (must be clearly indicated on the first page) or on a form provided by the Hoboken Division of Housing prior to the increase being implemented:

rules.title: Hoboken capital improvement surcharge tenant notice
rules.requirement: After the Board approves a capital improvement surcharge application, the landlord must personally serve tenants a standardized notice explaining the surcharge, base rent, apportioned surcharge, effective date and termination, and total rent, and file it with the Board and the Officer.
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords granted a capital improvement surcharge by the Board for dwellings under Article II of the Hoboken rent leveling chapter; newly constructed dwellings and buildings vacant since January 1, 1984 may be exempt.
rules.exemptions: Newly constructed dwellings and buildings completely vacant since January 1, 1984, whose eligibility for exemption is determined by the Regulation Officer and the Rent Regulation Officer (§ 155-16).
rules.quoted_span:
The landlord shall, upon approval by the Board of its capital improvement surcharge
           application, notify its tenants by personal service, on a standardized form, setting forth:

rules.title: Hoboken hardship rental increase requires Board approval
rules.requirement: A landlord may not impose any rent increase under Article II without Board approval. For a hardship increase, the landlord must serve each tenant notice of the appeal at least 20 days before the hearing and show it is not earning a fair return.
rules.coverage_conditions: Rent increases imposed on any tenant under Article II of the Hoboken rent leveling and stabilization chapter; newly constructed dwellings and buildings vacant since January 1, 1984 may be exempt.
rules.exemptions: Newly constructed dwellings and buildings completely vacant since January 1, 1984, whose eligibility for exemption is determined by the Regulation Officer and the Rent Regulation Officer (§ 155-16).
rules.quoted_span:
No landlord shall impose upon any tenant an increase in rent under this
           Article without first obtaining approval with the Board.

rules.title: Hoboken initial rental decontrol upon vacancy by bona fide condo/co-op owner-occupant
rules.requirement: When a bona fide condo/co-op owner-occupant who occupied the unit as principal residence for the previous two years vacates and offers it for rental, the unit is decontrolled solely to set the initial rent at the amount charged in the first lease after vacancy; it is otherwise fully subject to Chapter 155.
rules.key_value: initial rent = amount charged in first lease after vacancy
rules.coverage_conditions: Condo/co-op units whose owner continuously occupied the unit as principal residence for the previous two years; unit otherwise fully subject to Chapter 155.
rules.quoted_span:
In the event that an individual who qualifies as a bona fide CCOO vacates his/her condo/co-op
     unit and offers it for rental, said unit is decontrolled solely for the purpose of establishing the
     initial rent subsequent to the bona fide CCOO vacating.

rules.title: Hoboken COVID-19 temporary moratorium on rent increases
rules.requirement: During the COVID-19 pandemic state of emergency, rent and other charges (including surcharges and charges for parking, pets, furniture and deposits) may not be increased for property covered by Chapter 155; the moratorium is retroactive to April 1, 2020 and remains in effect until May 7, 2022.
rules.coverage_conditions: Any property covered by Chapter 155 of the Hoboken Code (rent leveling and stabilization).
rules.quoted_span:
The moratorium shall be made retroactive to April 1, 2020, and shall remain in effect until
           May 7, 2022.

rules.title: Hoboken rent ordinance just cause for eviction definition
rules.requirement: Under the chapter, 'just cause for eviction' means the landlord recovered possession of a housing space or dwelling for one of the reasons outlined in New Jersey State law (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-53 as amended).
rules.coverage_conditions: All dwelling units covered by Chapter 155, subject to the exemptions in § 155-2.
rules.quoted_span:
JUST CAUSE FOR EVICTION — The landlord recovered possession of a housing space or
     dwelling for one of the reasons outlined in New Jersey State law (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-53 as amended).

rules.title: Hoboken algorithmic rent fixing prohibition
rules.requirement: Landlords renting residential dwelling units in Hoboken may not price fix using algorithmic pricing — software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms that collect and analyze nonpublic competitor information to coordinate, recommend or implement rents, lease terms or occupancy levels.
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords who rent any residential dwelling unit, defined as any primary residence excluding medical/long-term care or detention facilities, in the City of Hoboken.
rules.exemptions: Medical/long-term care facilities and detention facilities are excluded from the definition of residential dwelling unit.
rules.quoted_span: Landlords who rent any residential dwelling unit (defined as any primary residence excluding medical/long-term care or detention facilities) in the City of Hoboken are prohibited from price fixing using algorithmic pricing.

rules.title: Jersey City Rent Control Ordinance 1-4 unit exemption
rules.requirement: The City administers the Rent Control Ordinance, Chapter 260; properties with one to four units are exempt from rent regulation, and owners meeting an exemption criterion may submit a Rent Control Exemption Request.
rules.coverage_conditions: Properties of 1-4 units are exempt from rent control; the ordinance's other exemptions are available on request.
rules.exemptions: All 1-4 unit properties are exempt from rent control; the ordinance provides certain exemptions for which an owner may submit a Rent Control Exemption Request.
rules.quoted_span: (Please Note: All 1-4 Unit Properties are exempt from rent control)

rules.title: Preventing Algorithmic Rent-Fixing in the Rental Housing Market
rules.requirement: Bars real estate lessors, agents and subcontractors from subscribing to or contracting with a service provider that collects competitor information to recommend rents, and bars service providers from facilitating agreements not to compete.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to real estate lessors of residential dwelling units, their agents and subcontractors, and service providers in Jersey City. Excludes licensed real estate agents acting per state regulations and owners acting only on their own properties.
rules.exemptions: Owners of multiple properties acting exclusively as to properties they control; licensed real estate agents complying with state regulations.
rules.quoted_span:
It is unlawful for any real estate lessor, agent, or subcontractor thereof, to subscribe to, contract with, or otherwise
exchange anything of value in return for the services of a Service Provider.

rules.title: Los Angeles RSO annual allowable rent increase (2025-2026)
rules.requirement: A landlord of an RSO-covered rental unit may raise rent by no more than 3% between July 1, 2025 and June 30, 2026. Beginning February 2, 2026, no additional percentage increase for utilities may be included.
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental units subject to the City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO); non-RSO properties are excluded.
rules.exemptions: Units not subject to the RSO (non-RSO properties); the page directs those landlords to the Housing Department for allowable increases.
rules.citation: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (L.A.M.C. §151.00 et seq.)
rules.quoted_span:
Annual rent increases for rental units subject to the City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO), effective
July 1, 2025, through June 30, 2026
is
3%
rules.conflict_note: Sources disagree: key_value: D042 says '3% (July 1, 2025 - June 30, 2026)', D041 says 'once every 12 months'

rules.title: LA RSO and JCO no-fault eviction relocation assistance
rules.requirement: For a not-at-fault eviction of an RSO or JCO unit, the landlord must file a Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD before serving notice and pay relocation assistance within 15 days. Not-at-fault causes include owner/relative occupancy, demolition and government order to vacate.
rules.coverage_conditions: Not-at-fault evictions of units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance or the Just Cause Ordinance. Mom and Pop properties (4 or fewer units) and single-family dwellings owned by a natural person may pay reduced relocation.
rules.exemptions: Resident manager replaced by another resident manager; eviction required by hazardous conditions from a natural disaster not caused by landlord negligence; landlord may offset accumulated rent against relocation assistance, except where a government order to vacate requires it.
rules.quoted_span:
All tenant not- at-fault evictions require payment of relocation assistance and the filing of a 
Declaration of Intent to Evict form with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) before 
evicting tenants from units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause 
Ordinance (JCO).

rules.title: Los Angeles RSO/JCO relocation assistance amounts
rules.requirement: A landlord who terminates a tenancy under the RSO or JCO must pay the tenant the relocation assistance amount set for the tenant's status (eligible or qualified) and length of tenancy within 15 days of serving the written eviction notice.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants whose tenancy is terminated under the RSO or the JCO; amount depends on eligible vs qualified status and length of tenancy. Single-family dwellings owned by a natural person with four or fewer units receive one month's rent.
rules.exemptions: Relocation offset: a landlord may offset the tenant's accumulated rent against relocation assistance, unless the termination is required by a governmental order to vacate or comply for an unpermitted dwelling.
rules.interaction: Relocation payment above the RSO or JCO amount under Option 3 is regulated by state law.
rules.citation: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (L.A.M.C. §165.00 et seq.)

rules.title: Los Angeles RSO legal reasons for eviction and relocation assistance
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict an RSO tenant only for the listed at-fault or no-fault reasons; no-fault evictions require relocation assistance, and any termination notice must be filed with LAHD within three business days of service.
rules.coverage_conditions: All rental units subject to the City's Rent Stabilization Ordinance.
rules.citation: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (L.A.M.C. §151.00 et seq.)
rules.quoted_span: Give the tenant a 30-day and 60-day written notice (some evictions require 120-day notice or up to a 1-year extension).

rules.title: Los Angeles RPO standardized relocation payments for new construction displacement
rules.requirement: A landlord displacing lower income households by demolishing their units for new construction must pay at least the standardized RPO relocation amounts, increased only if the State Housing Crisis Act or the RPO require more.
rules.coverage_conditions: Only low, very low and extremely low income households displaced by demolition of their units for new construction; above low income tenants receive the RSO or JCO amounts.

rules.title: Los Angeles security deposit interest ordinance
rules.requirement: A landlord subject to California Civil Code § 1950.5 must pay annual interest on security deposits held at least one year, at either the rate set by the Rent Adjustment Commission or the actual interest earned.
rules.key_value: RAC rate or actual interest earned, annually
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords subject to California Civil Code § 1950.5 who hold security deposits for tenants; mobile home parks are excluded.
rules.exemptions: Mobile home parks.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord who is subject to the provisions of Section 1950.5 of the California Civil Code shall pay annually interest on all security deposits held for at least one year for their tenants as follows:

rules.title: Los Angeles source-of-income discrimination prohibition
rules.requirement: A person offering, renting or listing a housing accommodation may not refuse to rent, renew or execute documents, apply different terms such as rates or damage deposits, or terminate a tenancy because of a person's source of income, including Section 8 vouchers and other rental assistance.
rules.coverage_conditions: All dwelling units, efficiency units, guest rooms, suites, duplexes, condominiums, single family residences and mobile homes in the City of Los Angeles, rented or offered for rent for living or dwelling purposes.
rules.quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful for any person offering for rent, renting, or listing any housing accommodation to do or attempt to do any of the following:

A. Based upon a person’s source of income, refuse to rent or lease, or to continue to rent or lease, a housing accommodation

rules.title: Los Angeles motion to study a ban on algorithm-based rent-setting software
rules.requirement: Would instruct the Los Angeles Housing Department to report on the number of owners and managers using algorithm-based software to set rents and on the feasibility of banning that software in the City.
rules.quoted_span:
I THEREFORE MOVE that the City Council instruct the Los Angeles Housing Department to 
report on the number of ownership and management entities that are using algorithm-based 
software to establish rents and the feasibility of instituting a ban on the use of this software to set 
rents in the City.
